description: Key facts on past DRAM downturns (2018-2019 and 2022-2023): contract/fixed price peaks and troughs (DRAMeXchange DDR4 8Gb PC DRAM fixed transaction price unless stated), timing of first declines, and production/wafer-input cuts by Micron, SK hynix, Samsung.

rows.event: DDR4 8Gb PC DRAM fixed (contract) price at cycle peak
First monthly fixed-price decline (end-Oct print)
TrendForce: PC DRAM contract prices turned down sharply after 9 straight quarterly rises; 8GB module 4Q18 $68->$61 (-10.3% q/q)
November 2018: some contracts cut twice in the month, moved to monthly terms; 8GB module -1.6% m/m
December 2018 contract prices described as stable vs November; January 2019 forecast >=10% m/m drop; 1Q19 forecast ~-20% q/q
Micron guided FQ2-19 (Dec18-Feb19) non-GAAP GM 50-53% vs 59.0% in FQ1-19 -- first sharp guidance cut of the cycle
Monthly fixed-price decline streak ended: Jan 2020 first rise after 13 months of decline
DDR4 8Gb fixed price trough (Dec 2019), back-computed from Mar-2020 $2.94 and Jan/Feb/Mar 2020 increases (+1.07%,+1.41%,+2.08%)
Peak-to-trough decline, DDR4 8Gb fixed price ($8.19 -> ~$2.81)
Micron announced ~5% DRAM and ~5% NAND production cuts
Micron deepened NAND cut to ~10% for 2019; kept DRAM -5%; capex cut by $1.5bn to ~$9bn

SK hynix (Q1-19 results, Apr 2019) had planned >10% y/y NAND wafer-input cut; at Q2-19 results raised to 15% and announced DRAM output reduction (part of Icheon M10 moved to CMOS image sensors, effect from 4Q19 into 2020)
rows.value: NAND wafer input -15% y/y (2019); DRAM capacity reduced (no % given)

rows.event: Samsung did not announce production cuts in 2019 (Q2-19 results made no mention of capacity cuts)
DDR4 8Gb fixed price peak
First fixed-price decline after peak
Steep fall: October 2022 fixed price
SK hynix cut 2023 capex by >50% from ~20tn won in 2022 and said it would reduce production
Micron cut DRAM and NAND wafer starts ~20% vs prior quarter (after ~50% capex cut)
Samsung officially announced memory production cut to a 'meaningful' level -- first official admission after saying no artificial cuts
rows.value: official cut (no % given); Q1-23 company OP ~0.6tn won

rows.event: SK hynix announced additional 5-10% NAND output cut for 2023; DRAM output also expected to decline
DDR4 8Gb fixed price trough
Peak-to-trough decline, DDR4 8Gb fixed price ($4.10 -> $1.30)
First fixed-price rise in 27 months (after Samsung output cuts)
Lag: peak (Jul-2021) to Samsung official cut (Apr-2023)
Lag: Samsung official cut (Apr-2023) to first price rise (Oct-2023)

notes: Late-2018 episode: per TrendForce/DRAMeXchange the contract decline began in OCTOBER 2018 (DDR4 8Gb fixed price -10.7% to $7.31), not December; December 2018 prints were roughly flat vs November, and the steep leg came in January-March 2019 (~-20% in 1Q19 forecast). Spot prices had been falling since early 2018. Newdaily's '13-month decline ended Jan 2020' implies the uninterrupted monthly decline streak counted from about Dec 2018/Jan 2019, which may be the source of the 'from December' framing. The 2019 trough level (~$2.81, Dec 2019) is back-computed from reported 2020 monthly changes, not directly quoted -- marked derived. Samsung made no official DRAM cut in 2018-2019 (SK hynix and Micron did). In 2022-2023, Micron cut first (Nov 2022), SK hynix cut capex/output (Oct 2022, Jul 2023), Samsung officially cut in Apr 2023; prices bottomed Jul-Sep 2023 and rose from Oct 2023. Percent wafer-input cuts by Samsung/SK hynix for DRAM were not officially quantified (press estimates exist but not captured here).
